newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower despite Iraq.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower despite Iraq.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended lower Tuesday, after giving back some early firmness seen on news of the U.S. attack on Iraq.

"After the July-August recovery in gold began to lose momentum last week, with producers willing to sell near $390 basis spot, I think you're seeing some funds lightening up again, and I wouldn't be surprised if we test $385.00 again," Mitsui USA bullion dealer Greg Drury said.
COMEX December gold ended down 80 cents at $390.50 an ounce, after trading in a $392.20-$390.40 range, on total estimated gold futures volume of 17,000 lots.
In New York bullion trade, spot gold ended quoted $386.15/386.55, from a London afternoon fix Tuesday at $386.60, and a Friday close in New York at $386.50/387.00.
COMEX December silver ended down 4.2 cents at $5.208, after trading between $5.290 and $5.205.
If the sharp rise in crude oil prices following the U.S. attack on Iraq persists, there is a possibility of higher world inflation which would be supportive for precious metals, analysts said.
